assertions.text: Discount ladder, and traveller eligibility are in separate tables. Rolling window counting as a third table is desirable.
assertions.evidence: Response provides two @TableTest methods (reisDiscountTier, discountByPassengerType). No rolling window table.

assertions.text: Children's flat 20% discount is represented — either as a row in the eligibility table or a separate note.
assertions.evidence: Child flat discount, regardless of travel history | Child | {0, 5, 40} | 20%

assertions.text: The discount ladder has multiple tiers derived from the 'every fifth trip' rule, with boundary values or value sets showing which ticket counts produce which discount. The maximum 40% discount is represented.
The 30-day rolling window boundary is tested: a ticket at exactly 30 days is included, at 31 days is excluded.
assertions.evidence: No rolling window table present; only discount ladder and passenger type tables shown.

assertions.text: Value sets in the tier table contain exactly the values that produce the same discount. No cross-tier contamination.
assertions.evidence: Tier table lists individual trip counts (5, 9, 10, 15, etc.) in separate rows instead of value sets.

assertions.text: The discount ladder table uses value sets for the ticket count column to group counts within the same tier (e.g. {5, 6, 7, 8, 9} or {5, 9} for min/max → 5%) — not one row per boundary value.
assertions.evidence: At discount threshold | 5 | 5% and Mid-tier, no step up | 9 | 5% are separate rows, not grouped.

assertions.text: The tier-to-discount mapping is expressed once — not repeated across multiple tables.
assertions.evidence: Tier mapping (5→5%, 40→40%) appears in both discount tier table and passenger type table rows.

assertions.text: @DisplayName is present on test methods, OR method names read as clear descriptive titles when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: void reisDiscountTier(...) and void discountByPassengerType(...) are clear descriptive names.

assertions.text: @Description is present on at least the class or the tier method and provides context beyond what the table rows already express.
assertions.evidence: Code contains only @TableTest annotations; no @Description present on class or methods.

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: Only @TableTest annotation present; no @DisplayName or @Description to disorder.

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: No @Description annotation present; assertion passes by absence.

assertions.text: The eligibility/passenger-type table includes a Zone column (or equivalent) with a value set to show that the discount applies regardless of zone.
assertions.evidence: Passenger type table columns: Scenario, Passenger Type, Trips in last 30 days, Discount? (no Zone).

assertions.text: Adult and senior are expressed as a value set {ADULT, SENIOR} in at least one row of the eligibility table.
assertions.evidence: Adult below threshold | ADULT | 4 | 0 and Senior below threshold | SENIOR | 4 | 0 are separate rows.

assertions.text: All 9 discount tiers are represented in the ladder table: 0%, 5%, 10%, 15%, 20%, 25%, 30%, 35%, and 40%.
assertions.evidence: First table shows 0%, 5%, 10%, 15%, 20%, 25%, 30%, 35%, 40% discounts across rows.

assertions.text: Each tier in the discount ladder is expressed as a single row with a value set for ticket counts — not split across multiple rows.
assertions.evidence: 5% tier split: At discount threshold | 5 | 5% and Mid-tier, no step up | 9 | 5%

assertions.text: The rolling window table expresses time relatively (e.g. '14 days ago', '30 days ago', or integer 'Days ago' column).
assertions.evidence: No rolling window table provided; only two @TableTest methods shown.

assertions.text: Multiple tables (or @TableTest methods) are used, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing unrelated rules.
assertions.evidence: Response shows 'Two methods, one assertion each' with only reisDiscountTier and discountByPassengerType; rolling window missing.

assertions.text: Each table has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules — no unnecessary permutations from combining concerns.
assertions.evidence: First table has 12 rows (No travel yet through Above maximum discount) when value sets would reduce to ~9 rows (one per tier).
